verbose_prose.definition: Prose (prompt, tool description, doc, comment, UI copy) longer than it needs to be: repetition, filler, rationale nobody needs.

docstring_restates_code.definition: A docstring or comment that restates what the code already says.

comment_narrates_edit.definition: A comment that describes the change or its history instead of the code.

comment_low_value.definition: A comment that names nothing on its own line, points elsewhere, or cannot reach the reader it is meant for.

naming.definition: A name that misdescribes what a value holds or a function does, lacks a verb, overclaims, or needs outside context to judge.

new_jargon.definition: A coined word, metaphor or undeclared term (mint, figure, ledger, book, landed, area, attacker) used where the project already has a word, or never declared.

banned_word.definition: The reviewer asks for a word to be removed everywhere: a candidate BANNED_WORDS entry.

synonym_rotation.definition: More than one name for one concept, such as a list of alternate spellings.

fabrication_or_fallback.definition: A silent fallback, default, or try-each-location lookup where the code should be explicit or fail.

should_raise.definition: Returns a message, None or a soft refusal where the code should assert or raise.

optional_deferral.definition: An optional field or parameter that defers a decision, or a field left optional that was agreed to be required.

silent_skip.definition: A skipped test or check that hides a failure.

diff_too_big.definition: The change is larger than the ask and should be split or shrunk.

scope_creep.definition: The PR adds features, fields, validation or concepts nobody asked for.

needless_abstraction.definition: A new type, record, class, field, method, module or agent the design does not need, or one that duplicates an existing concept.

reinvents_existing.definition: Re-implements a primitive, model or class that already exists in the codebase instead of calling it.

overcomplicated.definition: Logic more complex than the problem: extra flags, branches, wrappers, or helpers around a one-line expression.

two_sources_of_truth.definition: The same fact declared twice (two lists, two fields, two models) that must agree, with nothing enforcing it.

hardcoded_fact.definition: A literal, such as an agent count, that should be derived from the source of truth in code.

wrong_type.definition: A value modelled with an imprecise type: an int range for a closed set, a str for an ID.

enforce_by_type.definition: The reviewer asks for an invariant to be enforced by the type checker or at construction, not by a runtime check.

dict_any.definition: dict[str, Any] or loosely typed objects where a typed model belongs.

layering.definition: Code placed in the wrong layer or package: presentation in a service, validation outside its model, a feature under the wrong package.

dead_code.definition: Code or a feature nothing uses, or that the reviewer wants deleted rather than kept or moved.

data_model_clarity.definition: What a record stores and where state lives: derivable or duplicate fields, missing ids, record lifecycle.

llm_contract.definition: How work is split between code and the LLM: derive in code instead of asking the model, enforce in the schema instead of in prompt prose.

product_copy_wording.definition: The words of user-facing or model-facing copy (role names, rubric wording, framing), as distinct from its length.

contradicts_agreed_decision.definition: The diff goes against something already agreed with the reviewer.

incomplete_migration.definition: A concept agreed for removal still has live callers in the diff.

overclaim.definition: Prose (PR text, reply, prompt) claims something the diff or the data does not support.

request_not_done.definition: A change the reviewer asked for was not made.

correctness_bug.definition: A behavioural bug or a missed edge case.

test_restates_code.definition: A test that only restates trivial code or data.

tests_missing_or_weak.definition: A needed test is absent or does not exercise the behaviour.

display_readability.definition: A value shown to readers in a machine format.

design_disagreement.definition: The reviewer disagrees with a product or architecture choice; judging it needs product context.

review_guide_quality.definition: What the PR should flag for the reviewer: trade-offs and tensions to call out.

pr_description_quality.definition: The PR description is missing, wrong or hard to review.

missing_link.definition: A reference without a clickable link.

ui_in_prose.definition: A UI proposal described in prose instead of a rendered mock-up.

x_not_y_padding.definition: An 'X, not Y' construction where 'not Y' adds no information.

ascii_diagram.definition: A diagram drawn in ASCII instead of Mermaid or a table.

arch_test_weakened.definition: An arch test relaxed, skipped or allowlisted.

question_only.definition: The reviewer asks for an explanation; no change is requested outright.

agent_decision_flag.definition: NOT the user: an inline comment the coding agent posted under the user's login to flag a decision (the review guide).

agent_reply.definition: NOT the user: the agent's reply on a review thread, posted under the user's login.

agent_pr_update.definition: NOT the user: a conversation comment by the agent (review-guide update, CI note, closing note).

agent_review_summary.definition: NOT the user: a review body the agent submitted with its decision flags.

rule_canonical.RC_no_needless_type: Don't add a type, record, class, field or agent the design doesn't need.
rule_canonical.RC_name_says_what: A name says exactly what the value holds or the function does.
rule_canonical.RC_prompt_brevity: Prompt and tool copy says each thing once, briefly; cut the rest.
rule_canonical.RC_reuse_existing: Reuse the existing primitive, type or class; don't hand-roll a copy.
rule_canonical.RC_project_vocabulary: Use the project's words; no coined jargon, metaphors or narrowing role names.
rule_canonical.RC_llm_contract: Derive and enforce in code or schema; ask the LLM only what code can't do.
rule_canonical.RC_prompt_accuracy: Prompt copy states the true purpose in plain words and matches the code.
rule_canonical.RC_layer_placement: Put code in the layer that owns it: lifecycle in services, wording in web, validation on models.
rule_canonical.RC_cut_unrequested: Cut features, fields and concepts nobody asked for.
rule_canonical.RC_data_model_minimal: Store no derivable or duplicate fields; keep records minimal and linked by id.
rule_canonical.RC_delete_dead: Delete dead code and dead features instead of maintaining them.
rule_canonical.RC_simplest_logic: Prefer the simplest logic: no flags, wrappers or helpers for trivial code.
rule_canonical.RC_honor_decisions: Follow what was agreed: don't change agreed rules, finish agreed migrations.
rule_canonical.RC_precise_types: Use precise types: models over dict[str, Any], enums for closed sets, checked exhaustiveness.
rule_canonical.RC_one_source_of_truth: Declare each fact once; derive counts and classifications from it.
rule_canonical.RC_fail_loudly: Raise or be explicit; no refusal strings or try-each-location fallbacks.
rule_canonical.RC_claims_match_diff: Say only what the diff does; do what the reviewer asked or say why not.
rule_canonical.RC_correctness: Check edge cases such as fully cached runs and links that must resolve.
rule_canonical.RC_tests_trivial: Don't write tests for trivial helpers.
rule_canonical.RC_readable_display: Show values to readers in human-readable form.
rule_canonical.RC_call_out_tradeoffs: Call out behaviour-versus-code tensions explicitly for the reviewer.
rule_canonical.RC_domain_judgment: Not a portable rule: a product or domain judgment call (rubric wording, what a concept means).
rule_canonical.RC_explain_state: Not a rule: a request to explain state, data flow or a reason.

field_notes.author: human = the user typed it; agent = the coding agent posted it under the user's GitHub login. Decided by reading each comment.
field_notes.severity: null for praise and for agent comments.
field_notes.gateable: deterministic = a string, AST or diff-size check could catch it; judge = an LLM reading the diff and thread could; none = needs the user's private context. null for agent comments.
field_notes.rule_canonical: a hand-assigned cluster of the per-comment rule, used to count repeated rules.
field_notes.echo_themes: agent comments only: a correction the agent reports. echo_kind: explicit (names the user, owner or review, or says you were right), implied (mentions corrections without saying whose), closing_note (closes or supersedes the PR, no attribution).
